headline: Mehidy Hasan Miraz: Bangladesh missed World Cup due to political issues
summary: The ODI captain reflects on the team's absence from the 20-team tournament, calling it unfortunate for the players and younger talents.
details: Bangladesh ODI captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz has stated that the Tigers were deprived of the opportunity to play in a World Cup because of "political issues."
Speaking to REVSportz, Miraz expressed that it was unfortunate for the players, especially younger ones, who dream of playing in the marquee event.
The team had been replaced by Scotland after refusing to tour India for the tournament, citing safety concerns amid deteriorating political relations between the two countries.
Bangladesh had requested the ICC to shift their matches to co-host Sri Lanka, but the request was rejected as it was not feasible to alter the schedule so close to the start date.
The standoff was further complicated by the reports that fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman was released by IPL franchise Kolkata Knight Riders following directives from the BCCI.
Despite the diplomatic tensions, India is scheduled to tour Bangladesh in September for three ODIs and three T20Is, a series which Miraz says the team is excited about.
caption:
“Every player dreams of playing in a World Cup.” 

Mehidy Hasan Miraz reveals why Bangladesh missed the tournament.

Bangladesh ODI captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz has stated that the Tigers were deprived of the opportunity to play in a World Cup because of "political issues."

Speaking to REVSportz, Miraz expressed that it was unfortunate for the players, especially younger ones, who dream of playing in the marquee event.

The team had been replaced by Scotland after refusing to tour India for the tournament, citing safety concerns amid deteriorating political relations between the two countries.

Bangladesh had requested the ICC to shift their matches to co-host Sri Lanka, but the request was rejected as it was not feasible to alter the schedule so close to the start date.

The standoff was further complicated by the reports that fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman was released by IPL franchise Kolkata Knight Riders following directives from the BCCI.

Despite the diplomatic tensions, India is scheduled to tour Bangladesh in September for three ODIs and three T20Is, a series which Miraz says the team is excited about.
